title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This is the 1986 'Analysis situs' draft on combinatorial or stratified 'figures'. M is a set of strata ('multiplicités'). A figure F is a union, or Sup, of strata X ∈ M. Three relations appear:
- G ≤ F: G is a sub-figure of F.
- G ≼ F: a stronger sub-figure relation. From the context it is probably 'open' or 'saturated' sub-figure, the kind that is stable under the induction statement C6.
- G ≪ F: defined by the existence of F̄ with G ≤ F̄ ≼ F.

On p.76 Grothendieck takes G ≪ F and a sub-figure F' ≤ F. He defines G' = G ∩ F̄', the sub-figure of G induced by F', i.e. the strata of G that 'satisfy' F'. He states that G' is an infimum of G and F' for ≪.

This page proves that claim.
1. Write G ≤ F̄ ≼ F.
2. Apply C6 (induction is compatible with ≼): from F̄ ≼ F and F' ≤ F one gets F̄' ≼ F', and also G' ≤ F̄' with G' = G ∩ F̄'. In particular G' ≪ F'.
3. To show the inf property, take K with K ≪ G and K ≪ F'; one must show K ≪ G'. He plans to reduce to two special cases, G ≼ F and G ≤ F.

Lemma 1 (case G ≼ F, G' the induced figure). Suppose K ≪ G and K ≪ F'.
1. Write K ≤ Ḡ ≼ G ≼ F, so by transitivity Ḡ ≼ F.
2. By C6(b) applied to Ḡ ≼ F and F' ≤ F, the induced Ḡ' satisfies Ḡ' ≼ G' ≼ F'.
3. So it suffices to prove K ≤ Ḡ'. Since K is the Sup of its strata, this reduces to: for every stratum X ≤ K, X ≤ Ḡ'.
4. Such an X satisfies X ≤ Ḡ and X ≪ F'. By C6(b), Ḡ' consists of exactly the strata of Ḡ satisfying F', so X ≤ Ḡ'.

Lemma 2 (case G ≤ F) is begun on p.78 and abandoned ('J'abandonne…', with a reference back to p.51). Grothendieck then notes that F' ↦ G' commutes with arbitrary Sup and Inf≤. He moves on to a proposition: X ≪ F implies X ⋘ Y for some stratum Y ≤ F, and there is a smallest such Y.

Purpose: build the order-theoretic calculus (a lattice structure) of sub-figures of a stratified object. This is part of the foundations of a 'tame' combinatorial topology.
errors: The step 'X ≤ Ḡ, X ≪ F' ⇒ X ≤ Ḡ'' relies on C6(b) identifying Ḡ' with the strata of Ḡ satisfying F'. It is only asserted by reference to C6 and is not verified on this page.

The overall inf claim is not completed. The general case is to be reduced to the cases G ≼ F and G ≤ F, but the reduction is not justified here, and Lemma 2 is abandoned on the next page. So the proposition remains unproved in this draft.
The p.76 side remark that G' = ∅ ⇔ G disjoint from F' is flagged by Grothendieck himself as 'non évident' and is left unproved.

ideas.what: Sub-figure induced on G by a sub-figure F' of F is an infimum for the relation ≪ (G ≪ F iff G ≤ F̄ ≼ F)
ideas.modern_name: Lattice / meet structure on posets of (closed/open) unions of strata in a stratified space; order-theoretic stratification theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: General stratified-space theory (Whitney, Thom, Mather); poset-of-strata viewpoint (e.g. Lurie's exit paths, Treumann) — no specific credit for this lemma
ideas.where_published: Programme of 'topologie modérée' only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); these Analysis situs notes are unpublished

ideas.what: Reduction of the inf property to the two cases G ≼ F and G ≤ F, using a base-change/induction compatibility lemma C6
ideas.modern_name: Stability of open/closed unions of strata under restriction (base change of stratifications)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine foundational order-theoretic lemma in an abandoned draft. It is of historical interest as part of the unpublished 'tame topology' programme, but the mathematical content is elementary and the proof is left unfinished.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 annotation likely reads 'G sous-figure d'une sous-fig. F̄ de F', not 'G [?] ligne d'un [?] sous-ens.'
'et ceci [?] aux deux cas particuliers où' likely reads 'et ceci on le ramène aux deux cas particuliers où'.
In Lemma 1, 'donc K ≪ G'' should read 'alors K ≪ G''.
'En effet, par [-déf-] ... on a' likely reads 'par définition on a K ≤ Ḡ ≼ G'.
'on a vu [?]' is better read as 'on doit voir que pour X ∈ M, X ≤ K ⇒ X ≤ Ḡ''. The underset reads 'd'où X ≤ Ḡ, X ≪ F''.
Vertical relation symbols in the diagrams are '∨|' (rotated ≤, i.e. lower row ≤ upper row), not '∨∨'.
Final line reads 'Or ceci résulte de C 6, (b) appliqué :'.
